identity.name: CMR GREEN TECHNOLOGIES L
identity.industry: Metals & Recycling / Secondary Aluminium — auto-grade recycler (liquid metal + alloy ingots + wrought billets)

summary.oneLiner: India's leading non-ferrous metal recycler and the largest player in the Indian secondary (recycled) aluminium market by installed capacity and revenue.
summary.business: CMR Green processes, manufactures and sells recycled aluminium alloys (in ingot and liquid form), zinc alloy ingots, aluminium billets and segregated furnace-ready scrap of stainless steel, copper, brass, zinc, lead and magnesium. It recycles used beverage can scrap and metal scrap procured domestically and globally (Asia, Africa, Middle East, Europe, Americas), supplying primarily automotive OEMs and Tier 1 companies through 13 strategically located recycling units.

one-line thesis: India's **largest aluminium recycler** (4× nearest competitor, ~45% share of India's automotive recycled aluminium, #12 in the world incl. China per ICRA) delivered FY26 revenue ₹8,640cr (+30%), EBITDA ₹449cr (+50%) and PAT ₹228cr (+47%), with a **structurally low but stable ~₹11,000/ton EBITDA** commodity model that management insists must be read per-ton, not as a %. The story is capacity + mix: 6.15→~7 lakh MTPA by FY27, two new plants (Shoolagiri EV park, 2nd Bawal) commissioning this year, and diversification beyond auto into wrought (billets/sheet ingots), beverage-can (Hindalco), and non-ferrous — riding EV-lightweighting (3× aluminium per EV) and the FY29 **EPR recycled-content mandate**. Watch: thin margins, scrap-import restriction noise, and ~₹166cr OCI mark-to-market on hedges.

> **⚠️ Volume figure discrepancy:** management stated FY26 total volume "increased 24% to **80,381 MT**" (Al 65,636 + non-ferrous 14,745). This is **internally inconsistent with the per-ton math** — EBITDA ₹449cr ÷ ₹11,000/t and PAT ₹228cr ÷ ₹5,580/t both imply **~4.0–4.1 lakh MT** for FY26, and an analyst (Vinayak Kariwal) referenced ~3.5 lakh MT in FY25 / ~2.9 lakh MT in FY22. The printed absolute tonnage looks **truncated/mis-transcribed**; the **growth rates (+24% total, +27% Al, +18% non-ferrous) are the reliable takeaway**, implying ~4 lakh MT FY26. Verify the absolute number next quarter.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Volume growth:** FY26 grew ~25%; **expect similar ~25% in FY27**; FY28 also "a good growth year" (no number committed).
- **Capacity:** ~6.05–6.15 lakh MTPA now → **~7 lakh MTPA by FY27** (~80% aluminium / 20% non-aluminium).
- **Capex FY27:** **~₹200cr** already committed.
- **EBITDA/ton:** currently ~₹11,000+; guided to "**continuously improve**" via scale, technology and new value-added products — **declined to quantify**. Analyst floated a 7% margin target (vs 5.2%); mgmt **reframed to ₹/ton, not %**, and would not commit a number.
- **Mix:** 80:20 Al:non-Al today; could drift to **~75:25** over time as both grow (Hindustan Zinc zinc-alloy MoU is part of this).
- **End-market tailwind:** auto +12% in first 2 months of FY27 (EV cars +18%, 2-wheelers +12%); aluminium content in EVs ~**3× that of ICE**.
- **Carbon credits:** **2.73 lakh tons in stock**, accumulating **70,000–80,000 t/yr**; **no revenue recognised** (no marketplace yet) — future optionality.
- **New billet/sheet-ingot plant:** "possibility high," team evaluating site/capacity — **not yet committed**.
order book & pipeline: Not an order-book business. Sells to **most Indian 2W/4W OEMs and most Tier-1 auto component suppliers**, either as single-source (liquid-metal-tied plants) or major supplier; "relationships as old as we are," very high repeat orders, "very predictable" sales driven by proximity. Non-auto customers: **Hindalco** (beverage-can liquid metal), **Jindal Stainless**, **Aurubis (Germany)**. Named auto customer: **Craftsman Automation** (incl. Sunbeam) — mgmt says CMR's share there has grown 2–3×.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Aluminium (81% rev, ~80% capacity):** liquid/molten metal + alloy ingots (auto, ~45% India recycled-Al share) + wrought **green billets & sheet ingots** (first-in-country recycled wrought producer; serves construction + solar-panel/solar sectors).
- **Other non-ferrous (19% rev):** stainless steel, zinc, lead, copper, brass, magnesium (+ some non-metallics). Scrap sourced jointly, so segment EBITDA is not split out.
- **Beverage-can recycling (Odisha, near Hindalco):** supplies recycled **liquid metal to Hindalco (a primary producer)** — strategic proof that recycling is displacing primary supply. Beverage cans are "100% recycled."
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Wrought (billets/sheet ingots)** — first recycled domestic producer; large customer acceptance; second plant "high" probability. Aided by **Nippon Light Metal JV** tech.
- **EV / future-mobility** — Shoolagiri (TN) plant inside an EV/future-mobility park; 3× aluminium content per EV (battery casings/trays, motor covers, extrusions/forgings, progressively bodies).
- **Non-ferrous diversification** — Hindustan Zinc **zinc-alloy MoU**; broader non-ferrous mix-up toward 75:25.
- **Primary→secondary substitution + EPR** — **EPR mandate compulsory from FY29** (recycled content starting 5–10%, rising to 60–70% in some products); products increasingly "designed for recycling." Recycling seen overtaking primary as the dominant source of new metal over time.
- **Carbon credits** — 2.73 lakh t banked, monetisable if/when a marketplace emerges.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Liquid-metal lock-in (the core moat):** metal delivered **24×7 online, directly** to the customer's plant → the customer "is tied with us at the hip," avoids re-melt cost, no realistic switching. **Patents** on (i) safe **road transport of liquid metal** and (ii) **process control at the customer's end** — explicitly cited to "maintain our dominance in the liquid metal space."
- **Scale + cost leadership:** **4× nearest competitor** by installed capacity, **#12 in the world incl. China** (ICRA), ~**45% share** of India's automotive recycled aluminium; economies of scale + trained-manpower-driven scrap segregation = quality + cost edge.
- **JV technology access, no royalty:** three Japanese JVs (Toyota Tsusho, Nikkei MC Aluminium, Nippon Light Metal) where **CMR is majority**, partners minority, and **no royalty is payable** — technology + marketing support at no licence cost.
- **IP / process:** **8 copyrights** on SOPs; strong IT/process integration built "bit-by-bit over two decades."
- **Sourcing reach:** buys scrap "from practically all six continents" — supply-chain resilience against single-geography scrap bans.
- **ESG/proximity network:** 13 plants sited near customers (E/W/N/S); #6 world on S&P Global aluminium sustainability index; ⅓ power from solar; zero-discharge plants; EcoVadis bronze (84th percentile).
margins & cost dynamics: Commodity conversion model — **~5.2% EBITDA / 2.6% PAT, but ~₹11,000 EBITDA and ~₹5,580 PAT per ton**. Mgmt insists on **₹/ton framing** because LME/aluminium prices swing the % denominator. **Auto pricing is monthly cost-plus pass-through** — any change in aluminium price or FX passes to the customer; the customer bears price movement **day 60–90**, but CMR must **hedge its own day-1-to-day-60 exposure** ("buy day 1, sell day 100"). All positions are hedged under a "very strong risk-management policy," so LME spikes (post Iran-US war) "ideally should not affect us." Margin-improvement levers: scale/volume, technology, customer-specific new alloys, and mix-shift into wrought/non-ferrous.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **FY27 capex ~₹200cr** committed; capacity **6.15 → ~7 lakh MTPA** by FY27.
- **Under construction, both commissioning in FY27:** (1) **Shoolagiri, Tamil Nadu** — inside an EV/future-mobility park; (2) **second Bawal, Haryana** plant — customer-driven.
- **Ramping:** newly operational **Tirupati** and **Jharsuguda** units (capacity-utilisation ramp).
- **Odisha beverage-can plant** — near Hindalco, supplies liquid metal to Hindalco.
- **Wrought billet/sheet-ingot plant** — first line running well; a **second such plant is "highly" likely**, under evaluation.
- **Hindustan Zinc MoU** — zinc-alloy plant (non-ferrous diversification).
- Track record: **7 plants in 7 years**, 13 total today.
capital allocation:
- IPO was a **pure Offer-for-Sale (₹630cr)** — no primary proceeds to the company; growth self-funded.
- FY27 capex ~₹200cr funded internally (no raise flagged); no dividend policy discussed on this first call.
- **₹166cr OCI** sits on the balance sheet as cash-flow-hedge MTM against future predictable sales — will net to zero / offset as physical prices move; not a P&L loss.
- Carbon-credit inventory (2.73 lakh t) is un-monetised optionality on the balance sheet.
risks & watch-items:
- **Thin margins** (5.2% EBITDA / 2.6% PAT) — small conversion spread; profitability hinges on volume + hedging discipline.
- **Scrap-import restrictions** (imports ~⅔ of scrap): UAE 4-month export ban (CMR doesn't buy from UAE); **EU** threatening a ban on scrap export to non-OECD countries **from ~May-2027** and a **15% export duty from Sep-2026**; US mulling restrictions (has 50% Al import duty). Mgmt view: India has **applied for an EU exemption**; complex/hard-to-process scrap ("needs human intervention") will keep flowing to India; duties partly borne by suppliers, partly passed to customers. Multi-continent sourcing = mitigant.
- **Aluminium price volatility** (post Iran-US war spike) — managed via hedging + monthly pass-through, but a persistent risk to the P&L via OCI.
- **Absolute-volume disclosure discrepancy** (see §2) — verify next quarter.
- **Value-added ramp execution** — wrought/non-ferrous mix-up and new-plant commissioning must land to lift ₹/ton.
- **No committed margin/EPS guidance** — mgmt declined to quantify EBITDA/ton improvement.
management quality / tone: Founder-led (Mohan Agarwal, 40 yrs in aluminium recycling; father Chairman Emeritus; two sons in the business) yet "owner-run + professional" with a CXO layer. Confident, detailed, **transparent on the commodity-margin reality** (pushed back firmly on the "take EBITDA to 7%" framing, insisting on ₹/ton), and candid on hedging mechanics and OCI. Slightly promotional on ESG/awards (Great Place to Work, DJSI #6, EcoVadis). Handled a **skeptical analyst** (Vinayak, alleging stagnant FY22–25 volumes vs customers growing 2–3×) by asserting continuous market-share gains and share growth at Craftsman/Sunbeam. First call, so no guidance track record yet.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **Read this as ₹/ton, not %** — the whole model. A 5% EBITDA business that is actually a stable ~₹11k/ton converter; the % will move with LME regardless of operations.
- **Recycler supplying a primary producer** (liquid metal to Hindalco) is the tell that secondary is structurally displacing primary — the long-run thesis, with **EPR (FY29)** the policy accelerant.
- **Liquid metal is the moat, not the ingot** — 24×7 online delivery + transport/process patents create genuine switching costs; ingots compete on quality/consistency only.
- **Carbon credits (2.73 lakh t, +70–80k/yr, un-monetised)** are a free option awaiting a marketplace.
- **Scrap-ban headlines are a recurring but manageable noise** — CMR buys the *complex* scrap others can't process, and sources from six continents; India has sought an EU carve-out.
- **IPO was pure OFS** — no fresh capital; the ~₹200cr FY27 capex is self-funded off ₹449cr EBITDA.

one_liner.body: India's leading non-ferrous metal recycler and the largest player in the Indian secondary (recycled) aluminium market by installed capacity and revenue.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Claims industry leadership as India's largest non-ferrous metal recycler and market leader in secondary aluminium, and "Pioneer in recycled liquid aluminium supply with Just in time (JIT) deliveries".
- Moat framed as "Barriers to Entry": scale, technology, sourcing network and manufacturing footprint; and as "Integral Manufacturing Partner" via long qualification cycles, customised alloy development, JIT liquid aluminium delivery and strategically co-located facilities.
- Customer franchise of 350+ customers with 17-20 years of relationships, serving leading automotive OEMs and Tier-I suppliers; FY26 geographical revenue mix India 96.6% / outside India 3.4%.
- Deck states CMR is the "ONLY PLAYER to have multiple Joint Ventures with global Japanese players", qualified as "Amongst the domestic peer companies set considered in the Aluminium recycling industry".
- Structural tailwinds cited: India aluminium consumption projected to double from 5 to 10 Mn tonnes over the next decade; EPR recycled-content minimums of 10% / 20% / 25% for aluminium / copper / zinc rising by FY31; CBAM regulation opening new domestic and export customers.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Aluminium (81% rev, ~80% capacity):** liquid/molten metal + alloy ingots (auto, ~45% India recycled-Al share) + wrought **green billets & sheet ingots** (first-in-country recycled wrought producer; serves construction + solar-panel/solar sectors).
- **Other non-ferrous (19% rev):** stainless steel, zinc, lead, copper, brass, magnesium (+ some non-metallics). Scrap sourced jointly, so segment EBITDA is not split out.
- **Beverage-can recycling (Odisha, near Hindalco):** supplies recycled **liquid metal to Hindalco (a primary producer)** — strategic proof that recycling is displacing primary supply. Beverage cans are "100% recycled."

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers (primary end market)
- Aluminium – 78.42% of FY25 revenue from operations
- Other metals (zinc alloy ingots + segregated scrap of stainless steel, copper, brass, zinc, lead, magnesium) – 21.58% of FY25 revenue
- Geographic mix FY25: North India 57.67%, South India 23.12%, West India 19.21%
- Cast alloy automotive segment – ~42-45% volume market share (FY25)
- Recycled aluminium industry overall – ~10-12% volume share (FY25)

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward: raw-material scrap is procured both domestically and globally from around 198 suppliers across 73 countries and six continents (United States, United Kingdom, New Zealand, Australia, Europe, Africa, South Africa, Thailand, UAE, etc.), with a dedicated US sourcing presence through a wholly owned subsidiary; imports are the majority of purchases (Outside India 73.15% of raw-material and traded-goods purchases in FY25 vs India 26.85%). Forward: the Company sets up manufacturing facilities adjacent to or on customer premises (some on customer-leased land) and supplies liquid/molten aluminium on a just-in-time basis within a ~20-25 km radius using patented transport technology and a dashboard integrated with customers' furnace levels, deepening customer dependence. Strategic alliances/joint ventures with Toyota Tsusho Corporation, Nikkei MC Aluminium and Nippon Light Metal support technology and market reach (subsidiaries CMRN 74% and CMRT 70%; Nippon Light Metal holds 20% in CMR NLM Eco for wrought-alloy billets).

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not an order-book business. Sells to **most Indian 2W/4W OEMs and most Tier-1 auto component suppliers**, either as single-source (liquid-metal-tied plants) or major supplier; "relationships as old as we are," very high repeat orders, "very predictable" sales driven by proximity. Non-auto customers: **Hindalco** (beverage-can liquid metal), **Jindal Stainless**, **Aurubis (Germany)**. Named auto customer: **Craftsman Automation** (incl. Sunbeam) — mgmt says CMR's share there has grown 2–3×.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Volume growth:** FY26 grew ~25%; **expect similar ~25% in FY27**; FY28 also "a good growth year" (no number committed).
- **Capacity:** ~6.05–6.15 lakh MTPA now → **~7 lakh MTPA by FY27** (~80% aluminium / 20% non-aluminium).
- **Capex FY27:** **~₹200cr** already committed.
- **EBITDA/ton:** currently ~₹11,000+; guided to "**continuously improve**" via scale, technology and new value-added products — **declined to quantify**. Analyst floated a 7% margin target (vs 5.2%); mgmt **reframed to ₹/ton, not %**, and would not commit a number.
- **Mix:** 80:20 Al:non-Al today; could drift to **~75:25** over time as both grow (Hindustan Zinc zinc-alloy MoU is part of this).
- **End-market tailwind:** auto +12% in first 2 months of FY27 (EV cars +18%, 2-wheelers +12%); aluminium content in EVs ~**3× that of ICE**.
- **Carbon credits:** **2.73 lakh tons in stock**, accumulating **70,000–80,000 t/yr**; **no revenue recognised** (no marketplace yet) — future optionality.
- **New billet/sheet-ingot plant:** "possibility high," team evaluating site/capacity — **not yet committed**.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Wrought (billets/sheet ingots)** — first recycled domestic producer; large customer acceptance; second plant "high" probability. Aided by **Nippon Light Metal JV** tech.
- **EV / future-mobility** — Shoolagiri (TN) plant inside an EV/future-mobility park; 3× aluminium content per EV (battery casings/trays, motor covers, extrusions/forgings, progressively bodies).
- **Non-ferrous diversification** — Hindustan Zinc **zinc-alloy MoU**; broader non-ferrous mix-up toward 75:25.
- **Primary→secondary substitution + EPR** — **EPR mandate compulsory from FY29** (recycled content starting 5–10%, rising to 60–70% in some products); products increasingly "designed for recycling." Recycling seen overtaking primary as the dominant source of new metal over time.
- **Carbon credits** — 2.73 lakh t banked, monetisable if/when a marketplace emerges.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Maintaining long-term customer relationships (many OEM/Tier 1 customers retained for up to ten Fiscals) driving recurrent business
- Revenue mix across manufactured products, traded products, sale of segregated scrap and job-work services
- Shift toward liquid aluminium supply (39.19% of volumes in FY25 vs 32.04% in FY23) reducing customer re-melting, oxidation losses and power/fuel cost
- Rising leverage: Net Debt/Equity moved 0.15 (FY23) to 0.36 (FY24) to 0.58 (FY25); Net Fixed Asset Turnover declined 11.36 to 9.31 to 8.14

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Commodity conversion model — **~5.2% EBITDA / 2.6% PAT, but ~₹11,000 EBITDA and ~₹5,580 PAT per ton**. Mgmt insists on **₹/ton framing** because LME/aluminium prices swing the % denominator. **Auto pricing is monthly cost-plus pass-through** — any change in aluminium price or FX passes to the customer; the customer bears price movement **day 60–90**, but CMR must **hedge its own day-1-to-day-60 exposure** ("buy day 1, sell day 100"). All positions are hedged under a "very strong risk-management policy," so LME spikes (post Iran-US war) "ideally should not affect us." Margin-improvement levers: scale/volume, technology, customer-specific new alloys, and mix-shift into wrought/non-ferrous.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- IPO was a **pure Offer-for-Sale (₹630cr)** — no primary proceeds to the company; growth self-funded.
- FY27 capex ~₹200cr funded internally (no raise flagged); no dividend policy discussed on this first call.
- **₹166cr OCI** sits on the balance sheet as cash-flow-hedge MTM against future predictable sales — will net to zero / offset as physical prices move; not a P&L loss.
- Carbon-credit inventory (2.73 lakh t) is un-monetised optionality on the balance sheet.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: CMR is broadening beyond its established cast alloy segment by entering the extrusion and rolled aluminium alloy segments, which management says expands its serviceable market by a further 0.34 million MT (extrusion) and 0.59 million MT (rolled). This is enabled by new recycling plants at Tirupati (Andhra Pradesh) and Odisha (Sambalpur); the East India (Sambalpur) facility began trial production in February 2025. The company positions these plants to let it address a wider spectrum of aluminium products across the recycling value chain, leveraging existing recycling expertise and automotive …

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position
moat.body:
- **Liquid-metal lock-in (the core moat):** metal delivered **24×7 online, directly** to the customer's plant → the customer "is tied with us at the hip," avoids re-melt cost, no realistic switching. **Patents** on (i) safe **road transport of liquid metal** and (ii) **process control at the customer's end** — explicitly cited to "maintain our dominance in the liquid metal space."
- **Scale + cost leadership:** **4× nearest competitor** by installed capacity, **#12 in the world incl. China** (ICRA), ~**45% share** of India's automotive recycled aluminium; economies of scale + trained-manpower-driven scrap segregation = quality + cost edge.
- **JV technology access, no royalty:** three Japanese JVs (Toyota Tsusho, Nikkei MC Aluminium, Nippon Light Metal) where **CMR is majority**, partners minority, and **no royalty is payable** — technology + marketing support at no licence cost.
- **IP / process:** **8 copyrights** on SOPs; strong IT/process integration built "bit-by-bit over two decades."
- **Sourcing reach:** buys scrap "from practically all six continents" — supply-chain resilience against single-geography scrap bans.
- **ESG/proximity network:** 13 plants sited near customers (E/W/N/S); #6 world on S&P Global aluminium sustainability index; ⅓ power from solar; zero-discharge plants; EcoVadis bronze (84th percentile).

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Thin margins** (5.2% EBITDA / 2.6% PAT) — small conversion spread; profitability hinges on volume + hedging discipline.
- **Scrap-import restrictions** (imports ~⅔ of scrap): UAE 4-month export ban (CMR doesn't buy from UAE); **EU** threatening a ban on scrap export to non-OECD countries **from ~May-2027** and a **15% export duty from Sep-2026**; US mulling restrictions (has 50% Al import duty). Mgmt view: India has **applied for an EU exemption**; complex/hard-to-process scrap ("needs human intervention") will keep flowing to India; duties partly borne by suppliers, partly passed to customers. Multi-continent sourcing = mitigant.
- **Aluminium price volatility** (post Iran-US war spike) — managed via hedging + monthly pass-through, but a persistent risk to the P&L via OCI.
- **Absolute-volume disclosure discrepancy** (see §2) — verify next quarter.
- **Value-added ramp execution** — wrought/non-ferrous mix-up and new-plant commissioning must land to lift ₹/ton.
- **No committed margin/EPS guidance** — mgmt declined to quantify EBITDA/ton improvement.

non_obvious.body:

- **Recycler supplying a primary producer** (liquid metal to Hindalco) is the tell that secondary is structurally displacing primary — the long-run thesis, with **EPR (FY29)** the policy accelerant.
- **Liquid metal is the moat, not the ingot** — 24×7 online delivery + transport/process patents create genuine switching costs; ingots compete on quality/consistency only.
- **Carbon credits (2.73 lakh t, +70–80k/yr, un-monetised)** are a free option awaiting a marketplace.

- **IPO was pure OFS** — no fresh capital; the ~₹200cr FY27 capex is self-funded off ₹449cr EBITDA.

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Ramp new plants at Tirupati and Odisha to enter the extrusion and rolled aluminium alloy segments beyond the existing cast alloy base.**
- **Move the East India (Sambalpur, Odisha) facility from trial production to full commercial production.**
- **Operate the 13 recycling facilities at their combined actual production capacity.**
- **Sustain/grow leadership in the cast alloy automotive segment and overall recycled aluminium market share.**
- **Expand solar power capacity installed or under Power Purchase Agreement.**
- **Grow supply of recycled liquid aluminium leveraging patented delivery technology and adjacent-to-customer facilities.**
- **Commission new recycling plants at Tirupati (Andhra Pradesh) and Odisha (Sambalpur) to address a wider spectrum of aluminium products across the recycling value chain.**
- **Enter the extrusion aluminium alloy segment, expanding the serviceable market.**
- **Enter the rolled aluminium alloy segment, expanding the serviceable market.**
- **Operate the 13 recycling facilities at combined actual production capacity of 605,850 MT (baseline capacity, growth expected from segment/plant expansion).**
- **Expand renewable energy use – solar power installed or under Power Purchase Agreement supporting decarbonization positioning.**
- **Continue growing liquid aluminium supply via customer-adjacent and side-by-side facilities to sustain long-term demand stability.**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Enter the extrusion and rolled aluminium alloy segments to expand the serviceable recycling market beyond the cast alloy segment
- Commission new plants at Tirupati (Andhra Pradesh) and Odisha (Sambalpur) to address a wider spectrum of aluminium products within the recycling value chain
- Leverage liquid aluminium supply capability and customer-adjacent footprint across automotive clusters for long-term demand stability
- Position as a critical enabler of the aluminium industry's decarbonization (recycled aluminium emits ~0.3 t CO2/t vs ~14 t for primary in India)

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [JVs] Three joint ventures with Japanese partners: CMR Nikkei India Private Limited (since 2012), CMR-Toyotsu Aluminium India Private Limited (since 2012) and CMR NLM Eco Aluminium Private Limited (since 2025, following the 2025 JV with Nippon Light Metal Co., Ltd., Japan); benefits cited are liquid aluminium supply and market-share gain via Toyota Tsusho reach, wrought alloy recycling with billet-casting technical know-how, and building a low carbon billet supply system.
- [Corporate history] 2021 Scheme of Arrangement with group companies; 2013 PE investment from Global Scrap Processors Limited; listing on both BSE and NSE completed in 2026.
- [Regulation/policy] Policy tailwinds cited include EPR recycled-content minimums by FY31, CBAM, and PM E-DRIVE, a Rs. 10,900 Cr scheme to boost EV adoption and domestic manufacturing; EV aluminium lightweighting intensity is put at ~3x that of ICE (battery casings, trays, motor covers, body structures).
- [Market sizing] India recycled aluminium market volumes given as FY25 2,164k tonnes rising to FY30F 3,715k tonnes, an 11.2% volume CAGR over FY26-30F, sourced to IMARC and ICRA Analytics.
